articles.titleFull: Does FAQ Schema Still Matter After Google Removed FAQ Rich Results?
articles.alt: FAQ Schema and AI Search — puzzle piece with search icon and digital network
articles.intro: Yes, FAQ schema still matters, but not for the reason most website owners built it in the first place. Google removed FAQ rich results — but the markup still feeds AI search engines that are fast becoming the primary discovery layer.
takeaways: Google removed FAQ rich results on May 7, 2026 — but did not deprecate FAQPage schema itself
AI systems like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews still read structured FAQ content
Rewrite thin 30-word FAQ answers into complete 80–150-word responses for AI citation readiness
India's AI search adoption is outpacing business preparedness — creating a wider competitive window

body.text: Yes, FAQ schema still matters, but not for the reason most website owners built it in the first place. Google stopped showing FAQ rich results in Search on May 7, 2026, which means the expandable question-and-answer dropdowns that used to appear under organic listings are gone for good. What Google did not do is deprecate the FAQPage markup itself. The schema still works, it still validates, and it is now read mainly by AI systems like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's own AI Overviews rather than by the classic Google SERP.

That distinction, between a display feature and a comprehension signal, is the whole story here. Understanding it is the difference between panicking over a Search Console report going blank and actually adjusting a content strategy for how discovery works in 2026.
What Exactly Changed on May 7, 2026

Google quietly added a note to its FAQ structured data documentation confirming that FAQ rich results no longer appear in Search results. There was no dedicated announcement blog post, just a documentation update, which is itself telling about how minor Google considers the change (Search Engine Land, May 8, 2026). The rollout is happening in three stages. FAQ rich results stopped showing in the SERP on May 7. In June 2026, Google is retiring the FAQ search-appearance filter, the FAQ rich result report, and FAQ support inside the Rich Results Test tool. In August 2026, FAQ rich result support disappears from the Search Console API entirely, so any dashboard or BigQuery pipeline pulling that data will start returning nulls (The HOTH, May 2026).

For most commercial sites, agencies, and blogs, this will feel like a smaller shock than the headlines suggest. Google had already restricted FAQ rich results to a narrow set of authoritative government and health websites back in August 2023, following widespread abuse where marketers bolted generic FAQ blocks onto pages purely to grab extra SERP real estate (Elementera, May 2026). The May 2026 change simply removes the feature for that last remaining group too. If a business lost its FAQ dropdown visibility years ago and never noticed, this update changes almost nothing for them operationally.
Should a Business Remove FAQ Schema from Its Site

No. Google has said explicitly that leaving FAQPage markup in place causes no problems, throws no errors, and triggers no manual action (Google Search Central documentation, referenced across multiple May 2026 reports). The schema was never confirmed as a Google ranking signal in the first place, so removing it will not move rankings, and keeping it will not create risk. The only thing that changes is that the code no longer earns a visual reward in Google's own results page.

What is worth doing instead of ripping the markup out is auditing whether the underlying FAQ content is actually good. If a page's FAQ section only ever existed to game a rich result, this is the moment that becomes obvious, because the cosmetic cover for weak content just disappeared (The HOTH, May 2026).
Do AI Search Engines Still Use FAQ Schema

They use the structure, even where they do not rely on the schema tag itself as a formal signal. Google's own AI features guidance states there is no special schema.org markup required for AI Overviews or AI Mode, but any structured data used should match the visible page content exactly (Google Search Central, cited in Elementera's May 2026 analysis). What AI systems do consistently reward is content that is already organized as clear, self-contained questions and answers, because that format mirrors how a user phrases a query to ChatGPT or Perplexity in the first place.

Practitioners tracking this directly are seeing the pattern play out. One AEO monitoring tool reported that sites with well-structured FAQ schema and answers written between 80 and 150 words are showing up more often in ChatGPT and Perplexity citations than sites that kept their answers short and telegraphic, a habit left over from writing for Google's old accordion display (SEOcrawl, May 2026). That is a meaningful shift in intent even if the markup itself is unchanged. FAQ content used to be written short because the rich result only had room for a snippet. Now that the recipient is more often a language model assembling a fuller answer, a complete response with context and supporting detail has a better shot at being lifted directly.

"FAQ content used to be written short because the rich result only had room for a snippet. Now that the recipient is more often a language model assembling a fuller answer, a complete response with context and supporting detail has a better shot at being lifted directly."
What This Means for India Specifically

India sits in an unusual position on AI search adoption. Reported adoption figures vary by source and methodology, but multiple 2026 industry analyses place India among the fastest-growing markets globally for AI-assistant use, with buyers increasingly asking tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity direct questions such as "best CA firm in Kochi" or "top real estate advisory in Mumbai" and acting on whichever handful of brands the AI names (Adexorb, 2026; SEONova, June 2026). Most Indian small and mid-sized businesses have done close to zero preparation for this shift, according to multiple India-focused AEO guides published in 2026, which means the competitive window for FAQ-driven AI visibility is currently wider in India than in more saturated markets like the US or UK.

This is exactly where the FAQ rich results removal creates an opening rather than a setback. Businesses that keep writing thin, rich-result-era FAQ answers will keep losing ground quietly. Businesses that rebuild their FAQ sections as genuinely complete, well-sourced answers are positioning themselves for a discovery layer that barely existed eighteen months ago and is still comparatively uncrowded in the Indian market.
The Practical Move

Keep the FAQPage schema if it is already implemented correctly and matches the visible page content. Stop treating it as a SERP-feature shortcut, since that feature is gone. Rewrite thin, thirty-word answers that were built to fit inside an old Google accordion into fuller, 80-to-150-word answers that stand alone as complete responses. Group questions by what a buyer genuinely needs to know, whether that is a definition, a comparison, pricing, timing, or eligibility, rather than padding a page with generic questions nobody asked. And treat this as one part of a broader shift, not a standalone fix, since FAQ structure only helps if the rest of the page is also written to be understood and cited by an AI system rather than just crawled by Google.
Frequently Asked Questions

Should I remove FAQ schema from my website after the May 2026 Google update?
No. Google has confirmed that FAQPage markup remains valid and causes no errors or ranking issues if left in place. The only change is that it no longer produces a visible rich result in Google Search.

Does FAQ content still help with SEO in 2026?
Yes. FAQ content still improves page clarity, reduces user friction, supports topical relevance, and helps both search engines and AI systems interpret what a page covers, even without the visible rich-result snippet.

Will other search engines or AI tools still use FAQ schema?
Google has removed FAQ rich results from its own Search experience specifically, but AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini continue to read and extract structured Q&A content, which is a separate mechanism from Google's rich-result display.

What happened to FAQ rich results before this 2026 change?
Google restricted FAQ rich results to a narrow set of authoritative government and health websites in August 2023, following widespread misuse where sites added generic FAQ blocks purely to gain extra space in search results. The May 2026 update removes the feature for that remaining group as well.

How should FAQ answers be written for AI search visibility in 2026?
Answers should be complete and self-contained, generally in the 80-to-150-word range, addressing one specific question directly without requiring the reader to consult other parts of the page for context.

Is this change different for businesses in India?
The underlying mechanics are global, but India's AI search adoption is growing faster than most markets while business preparedness for AI visibility remains comparatively low, which creates a larger near-term opportunity for Indian businesses that rebuild FAQ content properly now.

articles.description: Google removed FAQ rich results — but FAQPage schema still feeds AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews. Here's what changed, what to keep, and what to rewrite.

articles.titleFull: How Do AI Answer Engines Choose Which Sources to Cite, and How Can a Business Become One in India?
articles.alt: AI answer engines and citation strategy — abstract digital brain with search and data nodes
articles.intro: AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews each run their own citation logic, weighing signals like entity clarity, third-party validation, freshness, and source diversity differently, so there is no single "rank" a business can win across all of them. Getting cited means treating each engine as a separate discovery channel with its own rules, not optimizing for one universal AI ranking.
takeaways: Only 11% of domains are cited by both ChatGPT and Perplexity — each engine has its own editorial identity
85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party pages, not the brand's own website
ChatGPT cites fewer sources but extracts 4.2x more per source; Perplexity casts a wider net
India is roughly 18 months behind the US in AEO maturity — creating a temporary competitive window

body.text: AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews each run their own citation logic, weighing signals like entity clarity, third-party validation, freshness, and source diversity differently, so there is no single "rank" a business can win across all of them. Getting cited means treating each engine as a separate discovery channel with its own rules, not optimizing for one universal AI ranking.
That single fact changes how a business should think about visibility budgets. A page that gets cited constantly by Perplexity can be invisible to ChatGPT, and the reverse happens just as often.
Do the Major AI Engines Actually Cite Different Sources for the Same Question

Yes, and the divergence is large. A citation analysis covering roughly 680 million citations across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and Perplexity found that only 11% of domains were cited by both ChatGPT and Perplexity for comparable queries (Leapd, April 2026). A separate study of 34,234 AI responses recorded a 46-times difference in brand citation rates between platforms, with ChatGPT citing brands in just 0.59% of responses compared to 13.05% for Perplexity and 27% for Grok (Leapd, April 2026, citing a 2026 platform study).

The practical reading is that each engine has developed its own editorial identity: ChatGPT leans on Wikipedia and Bing's index, Perplexity leans heavily on Reddit and named expert authors, Claude favors technical documentation, and Google AI Overviews largely mirror its own existing search rankings (Munder Difflin, June 2026; Chudi.dev, 2026).

"Each engine has developed its own editorial identity: ChatGPT leans on Wikipedia and Bing's index, Perplexity leans heavily on Reddit and named expert authors, Claude favors technical documentation, and Google AI Overviews largely mirror its own existing search rankings."
Is Being Cited by AI the Same as Ranking on Google

No, and the gap is bigger than most SEO teams assume. Independent analysis puts overlap between Google's organic top 10 and AI citations at roughly 12 to 17%, meaning the large majority of what AI engines cite is not what appears on page one of a traditional Google search (Chudi.dev, 2026; BrightEdge, February 2026). Google AI Overviews is the one partial exception, since it draws primarily from Google's existing organic results, with one study finding 97% of its cited sources coming from the top 20 organic positions (AI Labs Audit, May 2026).

For ChatGPT and Perplexity specifically, a strong Google ranking is close to irrelevant to citation odds. These are two largely separate optimization problems that happen to share some underlying content-quality fundamentals.

"For ChatGPT and Perplexity specifically, a strong Google ranking is close to irrelevant to citation odds. These are two largely separate optimization problems that happen to share some underlying content-quality fundamentals."
What Actually Earns a Citation

Across the engines, seven signals show up repeatedly in 2026 research: crawler accessibility, structured content density, recency, cross-source agreement, schema and metadata that matches the visible page, third-party validation, and community discussion signals (SolCrys, May 2026). Third-party validation deserves particular weight. One analysis found that 85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party pages rather than a brand's own website, and that ChatGPT and Claude draw more than 93% of their citations from earned media rather than owned content (AuthorityTech, May 2026). That means a brand's own blog, however well written, is only one part of the equation. Independent coverage, community mentions, and expert-authored third-party pieces carry disproportionate weight in what the models choose to cite.

Freshness compounds this. Pages carrying accurate dateModified schema receive roughly 1.8 times more citations than static pages, but only when the update reflects genuinely new content rather than a cosmetic date change (Chudi.dev, 2026).
How Many Sources Does Each Engine Actually Cite, and Does That Change Strategy

It changes strategy significantly. Perplexity casts the widest net, citing a mean of roughly 16 sources per answer, but a 2026 study across 602 prompts and 21,143 citations found each individual citation contributes comparatively little extractable content. ChatGPT cites fewer sources, roughly 7 on average, but extracts about 4.2 times more language and evidence from each one it does cite (AuthorityTech, May 2026). The implication for content strategy is direct: a business optimizing for Perplexity should aim for broad discoverability and topical presence, since even a partial citation among 16 has value, while a business optimizing for ChatGPT needs deeper, more extractable, more complete pages, since a citation there does much more work per source.
How Should an Indian Business Approach This Differently

India is one of the fastest-adopting AI markets globally, with one 2026 analysis placing India's AI adoption rate at 59%, ahead of the UAE, Singapore, and China (Omnibound, May 2026), while separate industry estimates put ChatGPT's Indian user base at 15 to 20 million monthly active users and growing roughly 350% year over year (NaviGo Tech Solutions, 2026). At the same time, most Indian small and mid-sized businesses have done close to zero structured preparation for AI search visibility, according to multiple 2026 India-focused AEO guides (SEORevive, May 2026; Adexorb, 2026). That combination, fast-growing demand paired with low competitive saturation, is unusual and temporary. Practitioners estimate India is roughly 18 months behind the US in AEO maturity, which is a real head start for any business that moves now rather than waiting for the category to get crowded (SEORevive, May 2026).

One India-specific nuance worth flagging: Google product documentation and Google's Search Central guidance emphasize that AI Overviews and AI Mode require no special schema markup, only that any structured data used matches the visible content on the page exactly. That single rule applies globally, but it matters more in markets like India where teams are often tempted to over-invest in schema hacks rather than the underlying content quality that actually earns citations.
What a Business Should Actually Do About This

Prioritize third-party visibility over owned-content volume, since earned media and community mentions carry more citation weight than a business's own site. Keep crawler access open for GPTBot, PerplexityBot, and ClaudeBot rather than blocking them by default, which some Indian hosting setups do unintentionally. Write for depth and extractability if ChatGPT visibility matters most, or for breadth and topical presence if Perplexity-driven, high-intent B2B traffic is the priority. And treat freshness as a genuine content-quality signal rather than a checkbox, since a stale dateModified tag on unchanged content does not move citation rates.
Frequently Asked Questions

Do AI answer engines use the same ranking system as Google?
No. Only Google AI Overviews closely mirrors Google's existing organic rankings, with roughly 97% of its citations coming from pages already in the top 20 organic results. ChatGPT and Perplexity operate on largely separate citation logic, and a strong Google ranking does not reliably predict citation on either platform.

Which AI engine should a business prioritize for citations?
It depends on the goal. ChatGPT has the largest reach and rewards deep, extractable content from fewer, more authoritative sources. Perplexity rewards topical breadth and community presence, cites more sources per answer, and tends to drive higher-intent B2B traffic. Most businesses need a strategy for both rather than picking one.

Does a business's own website content matter for AI citations?
It matters, but less than most businesses assume. Independent research found 85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party pages, not the brand's own site, and ChatGPT and Claude draw more than 93% of citations from earned media. Owned content should be excellent, but third-party visibility is what moves citation frequency.

Is India behind other markets on AI search readiness?
Yes, on the business-preparation side specifically, even though Indian consumer AI adoption is among the fastest-growing in the world. Multiple 2026 industry analyses describe India as roughly 18 months behind the US in AEO maturity, which currently means less competition for businesses that invest in AI visibility now.

Do I need special schema markup to be cited by Google AI Overviews?
No. Google's own guidance states there is no special schema.org markup required for AI Overviews or AI Mode. Any structured data used should simply match what is visibly on the page.

How quickly can a business start showing up in AI citations?
Fixing crawler access and basic structural issues can produce measurable change within roughly 4 to 8 weeks, according to industry benchmarks, while competitive commercial queries and genuine third-party authority building take considerably longer and require sustained effort.

articles.description: AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews each use different citation logic. Learn how to get your business cited in India's fastest-growing AI search market.
